entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flattest word here: it registers that damage happened and passes no verdict, where *scar* insists the damage lasted.

entries.definition: a small congenital pigmented spot on the skin
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely descriptive: a pigmented spot carried from birth, with no suggestion of damage or fault.

entries.definition: an impression in a surface (as made by a blow)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Smallest of the impressions, and the word makes the blow sound trifling where *dent* concedes real force.

entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest of the damage words: the harm is over but permanently recorded, where *scratch* passes.

entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Damage dragged across a surface — broader than *scratch* and still shallow.

entries.definition: an indication of damage
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The slightest indication of damage in the set — thin and superficial where *scar* is permanent.

entries.definition: a skin lesion that is a diagnostic sign of some disease
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical and grave: the lesion is not merely present but read as evidence, the skin testifying to a disease.

entries.definition: (pathology) a firm abnormal elevated blemish on the skin; caused by a virus
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical naming for a raised growth, but abnormality is built into it — not the plain report *mole* makes.

entries.definition: elegance by virtue of fineness of manner and expression
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Places the elegance in fineness of manner and expression, praising a person's polish rather than any effect they make.

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Magnificence that dazzles, adding glitter where *grandeur* adds height.
examples: his ‘Hamlet’ lacks the brilliance that one expects

entries.definition: elegance in dress or behavior
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and flatly approving: elegance of dress or behaviour named in one blunt syllable.
examples: she has a lot of class

entries.definition: the quality of being beautiful and delicate in appearance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The homelier name for beauty in fineness, prettier and less lofty in sound than *delicacy*.

entries.definition: distinctive and stylish elegance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same stylish elegance with spirit in it, brisk and showy where *style* is merely distinctive.
examples: he wooed her with the confident dash of a cavalry officer

entries.definition: the quality of being beautiful and delicate in appearance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises beauty that is fine rather than bold, the softest note in a family that runs to *grandeur*.
examples: The delicacy of the lace made it look like frost on a window.

entries.definition: ceremonial elegance and splendor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Ceremonial splendour with a flourish on it — the dazzle the occasion throws off, where *pomp* is the display itself.
examples: entered with much eclat in a coach drawn by eight white horses

entries.definition: a refined quality of gracefulness and good taste
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain central name for the quality — gracefulness and good taste, with no dazzle asked of it.
examples: she conveys an aura of elegance and gentility
Lady Catherine is far from requiring that elegance of dress in us which becomes herself and daughter.
I never saw such capacity, and taste, and application, and elegance, as you describe, united.

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Elevated and imposing — splendour on a scale that asks to be looked up at.
examples: an imaginative mix of old-fashioned grandeur and colorful art

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The largest word here — grandeur and splendour taken together at full strength, with nothing held back.
examples: for magnificence and personal service there is the Queen's hotel

entries.definition: ceremonial elegance and splendor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Binds the splendour to ceremony, so the praise falls on the staging rather than on the thing staged.

entries.definition: elegance by virtue of being fashionable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Measures the elegance by fashion, approving of being current in a way *elegance* never is.

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Full-throated praise for the magnificent, glowing where *grandeur* towers.
examples: it is the university that gives the scene its stately splendor

entries.definition: the quality of being magnificent or splendid or grand
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The British spelling of *splendor*, identical to it in force.

entries.definition: distinctive and stylish elegance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Approving and self-assured: elegance with a signature on it, where *elegance* alone can be impersonal.
examples: she had no conversation, no style, no taste, no beauty

entries.definition: the humane quality of understanding the suffering of others and wanting to do something about it
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The warmest word in the set: understanding that already carries the will to do something, not merely to be moved.
examples: She was proud that in a cause of compassion and honour he had been able to get the better of himself.

entries.definition: tendency to be kind and forgiving
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest word for the disposition, warm and unceremonious where *mercy* makes the same forgivingness sound grave.
examples: Her kindness was such that she never held anything against him for long.

entries.definition: a disposition to be kind and forgiving
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Grave and elevated where *kindness* is homely, giving the same forgiving disposition the weight of a virtue.

entries.definition: mercifulness as a consequence of being lenient or tolerant
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Faintest approval here, since the mercifulness follows from being lenient or tolerant rather than from any felt impulse, so it can shade toward slackness.

entries.definition: the humane quality of understanding the suffering of others and wanting to do something about it
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise here, since the gloss makes it a humane quality, but the word tilts down toward the sufferer where *compassion* stands level.
